cards.explanation: The answer is False. Mist and early dew don't stick around, and that's the whole picture. God says their loyalty is "…like a morning mist, like the early dew that vanishes." Their loyalty doesn't last, friends. It disappears. (Hosea 6:4)

The answer is the prophets. God says, "…I have hewn them by the prophets; I have slain them by the words of My mouth…" The prophets carry His words, and those words cut deep. It's a sharp picture, so I'm keeping my mustache still for this one, friends. (Hosea 6:5)

The answer is the knowledge of God. God says, "For I desire mercy, not sacrifice, and the knowledge of God rather than burnt offerings." He puts knowing Him ahead of burnt offerings. A gift is nice, bakers, but He's asking for the person to know Him. (Hosea 6:6)

The answer is False. God says, "But they, like Adam, have transgressed the covenant; there they were unfaithful to Me." The people didn't keep it, friends. They broke it, and the verse names Adam alongside them. (Hosea 6:7)

The answer is a band of priests. God says, "Like raiders who lie in ambush, so does a band of priests; they murder on the way to Shechem…" That's a heavy verse, friends, and I won't joke about it. The text puts these priests right next to raiders, and I'll let it speak plainly. (Hosea 6:9)

The answer is True. God says, "In the house of Israel I have seen a horrible thing: Ephraim practices prostitution there, and Israel is defiled." It's a serious line, so I'll just say it plainly, friends. The word defiled is right there in the verse. (Hosea 6:10)

The answer is when He restores His people from captivity. God tells Judah, "…a harvest is appointed, when I restore My people from captivity." The timing is tied to what He does, bakers. After all the hard words, there's a bright spot right at the end of the chapter. (Hosea 6:11)

The answer is that it is exposed. God says, "When I heal Israel, the iniquity of Ephraim will be exposed…" Iniquity is sin, friends, and it comes out into the open. Healing and exposing show up in the same breath here. (Hosea 7:1)

The answer is False. God says they don't consider in their hearts that He remembers all their evil. Then He adds, "Now their deeds are all around them; they are before My face." They aren't taking it to heart, friends, but He sees it all. (Hosea 7:2)

The answer is king. The verse says, "They delight the king with their evil, and the princes with their lies." The people bring something to the court, and the court is glad to get it, bakers. It's a rough bit of work to be proud of. (Hosea 7:3)

The answer is that it stays hot without more fuel. The verse says the baker "…needs not stoke the fire from the kneading to the rising of the dough." The oven stays hot with no extra fuel, friends. In God's picture, that's what the people are like, burning all the way through. (Hosea 7:4)

The answer is mock. The verse says, "The princes are inflamed with wine on the day of our king; so he joins hands with those who mock him." The king ends up joining hands with the very ones who mock him, friends. That's a strange team-up. (Hosea 7:5)

The answer is that it blazes up. The verse says, "all night their anger smolders; in the morning it blazes like a flaming fire." It burns low all night and then blazes up by morning, bakers. Smoldering sounds quiet, but it isn't. (Hosea 7:6)

The answer is their rulers. The verse says, "All of them are hot as an oven, and they devour their rulers." The heat turns on the people at the top, friends. Then it adds, "All their kings fall…" (Hosea 7:7)

The answer is True. The verse ends with, "All their kings fall; not one of them calls upon Me." Nobody reaches out to God, friends, even as the kings go down. I think that's one of the saddest lines in the passage. (Hosea 7:7)
